description:
Team ORBIT D3 | Colombo

We are tackling “Abandoned but not Forgotten”, telling the stories of NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. Our lead is a full-stack developer, and we plan to turn forgotten rovers and landers into an interactive web story.

We’re looking for:
Creative storytellers, UI/UX and graphic designers, 3D/animation artists, and space-science enthusiasts.

Passion matters more than experience!
summary: Echoes of Space is an interactive educational web platform built by Team ORBIT D3 that brings the stories of NASA's historic hardware left on the Moon and Mars—Apollo 11 Eagle, Apollo 15 Lunar Rover, Opportunity, and Ingenuity—to school-age students through interactive mission trails and live NASA archive data.
details:
Echoes of Space is an interactive educational web platform built by Team ORBIT D3 for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("NASA's Discarded Equipment Storytelling"). Designed for school-age learners (ages 10–16), the website brings the stories of four historic NASA spacecraft left behind on the Moon and Mars—Apollo 11 (Eagle), Apollo 15 (Lunar Rover), Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—to life.

How It Works & Key Features:

- Three-Chapter Storytelling: Every mission follows a structured journey (Beginning -> Discoveries -> Legacy) to transform complex planetary engineering into clear, engaging narratives.

- Interactive Mission Trail Maps: Users click step-by-step through mission waypoints from launch to final signal, unlocking progress stars, milestone popups, "Did You Know?" facts, and final resting telemetry cards.

- Live NASA Archive Feed: Integrates the NASA Image and Video Library API to dynamically fetch authentic archival mission photos with official catalog IDs and credits.

- Lightweight & Accessible: Built using pure HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript with zero external frameworks or installation required, featuring responsive layouts (desktop, tablet, mobile) and reduced-motion accessibility support.
